resources.string: Open a GanttProject file (.gan) from your device or from a cloud folder such as Drive, Nextcloud or OneDrive.
The project has unsaved changes. Closing it without saving loses them.
Dates and duration are edited on the desktop: changing them here would not move dependent tasks, because the scheduler does not run on the phone.
GanttProject recalculates a summary task\'s progress from its subtasks, so it cannot be set here.
A milestone is either reached or not; it has no progress.
Leave empty to remove the value.
Please enter a number, for example 7.5.
Nothing recorded on this task yet.
This task has no stable identifier, so work cannot be recorded on it. Open the project once in GanttProject on a computer and save it.
%1$d stored records could not be read. Nothing was deleted; open the project on a computer before recording more.
Actual hours say %1$s h, the records add up to %2$s h.

This throws the measured time away.

Separated by spaces. Passed to exports unchanged.
Written into every booking made on this device — and therefore into the project file, which travels with it to whoever you share it with. Left empty, the records carry no name.
A record counts in the month its stretch started in, so a night shift belongs to the day it began on.

There is a way out that loses no recorded time: take the other version and carry this device\'s records into it. The plan, progress and assignments then come from the other version — those can be made again, hours cannot.
Keep the other version, carry my records over
Change a name in existing records

This reaches into what is already recorded, so it asks for more than the field above. The previous name, the date and your reason are written into the file: the original stays establishable and the change is visibly a later one.
Leave empty to remove the name. That is a change like any other and is recorded the same way.

Every resource is already assigned to this task.
How many hours this person actually works per day. Empty means the default of 8 hours.
Stock GanttProject ignores the utilisation percentage when scheduling, so it never reports this. The figure here is the sum of all assignments per day against this resource\'s hours per day.
Found in Toggl under Profile settings. It is stored encrypted on this device only and never written into the project file.

Nothing to write — every entry was already imported.
Remember these assignments for next time
Imported entries are recorded in the project file itself, so a second run — from this or any other device — cannot add the same hours twice.

Reads and edits GanttProject files (.gan) on Android.

Files are edited in place: settings, calendars, baselines and anything else this app does not know about are preserved untouched, so a project can move between phone and desktop freely.

Free software under the GNU GPL v3.
Changes are saved automatically when you leave the app or close the project.
The planned duration of %1$d working days does not match this effort. At the current assignment it would be %2$d days.
Assign a resource to see how many days this effort corresponds to.
Read-only — reopen it with “Open project” to be able to save
This file has changed since you opened it — someone else has saved in the meantime. Your own work is safe and stays on the phone. Overwriting now would discard their change.
Tasks that are running or start soon — tick them off and record time.
Tap to open the app and choose a project for this widget.
The project could not be read. Tap to open the app.
Open on the PC — nothing was changed
Server not reachable — nothing was changed
The change could not be saved
Nothing on this phone writes to the project file.
Edit here, where you can see the project and are asked before anything gets overwritten.
In the app and the widget
Also allows ticking tasks off and recording time straight from the home screen.
Editing is switched off for this device. You can turn it back on under Settings.

This project is a file in a synced folder. Nothing decides which of two competing changes is the real one: if you edit here and the desktop saves before the sync has caught up, your change is gone without a trace.

The app refuses to overwrite a file that changed since you opened it — but it cannot bring back a change that was overwritten somewhere else.

At risk are progress, the completed mark and hours you typed in by hand. Hours from the time tracker are safe: what was imported is recorded in the project file, so a lost change simply means those entries are offered again next time.

Enter a project folder, not the collection root — the root often allows browsing but refuses saving. Projects on a WebDAV server are version-checked on save. Without a server the app keeps using files from your device.
Connected. The server supports locking, so a project open on the PC cannot be overwritten from here.
The server answered, but there is no folder at this address. Check the path — the address was not saved.
Connected, but the server does not support locking. Conflicts will be detected on save, not prevented.
The address must start with https://. The password is sent with every request.
Signed in, but not allowed to use this folder.
No such folder on the server.
Someone has this project open on the PC. Your changes are safe and stay on the phone. Saving works again once it is closed there, at the latest after two hours.
The server did not report a version for this project, so it cannot be saved safely. Reopen it and try again.
The server could not be reached (%1$s).
No projects found on the server.
You are signed in, but this folder is not shared with your account. Open a project from a folder you have access to, or ask for it to be shared.
This project is no longer on the server. It may have been renamed or deleted.
The server address in the settings is not a valid address. Check that it holds only the address, for example https://example.com/projects/.

This server cannot check versions when saving, so it cannot tell your save apart from overwriting work that is not yours. Saving was not attempted. This usually means compression is switched on for the server or a proxy in front of it.
There is already a project of that name on the server. Choose another one — nothing was overwritten.
The project is written to the sync server under this name and you keep working on that copy. An existing project of the same name is not overwritten.
A second project is created on the server under this name. Your unsaved work goes into it; the original is left as it is.
Open on the PC right now
This project is open on the PC right now. You can read and edit it here — saving will be refused until it is closed there, at the latest after two hours.
